items.author: Blue Dog Coalition
items.title: Blue Dog Statement on Bipartisan Permitting Reform Agreement
items.summary: The House Blue Dog Coalition backed the Senate deal, citing its SPEED Act, and asked leadership to hold a November floor vote.

quote.text: We urge House and Senate leadership to bring this bill to the floor for a vote in November.
quote.speaker: Blue Dog Coalition

items.outlet: Office of Sen. Edward J. Markey
items.author: Sen. Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.)
items.title: Senator Markey Statement on Bipartisan Permitting Reform Proposal
items.summary: Markey said he was still reviewing the text, warned against locking in more fossil fuels and locking out communities, and did not take a position.

quote.text: I’m still reviewing text of this proposal, and I will be looking closely at the details.
quote.speaker: Sen. Edward J. Markey

items.outlet: Senate Environment and Public Works Committee
items.author: EPW Majority
items.title: What They're Saying: Bipartisan Permitting Reform Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
items.summary: EPW's roundup of endorsements for the bill, including a governors' joint statement, the National Governors Association, labor leaders, energy producers and nonprofits.

quote.text: a broad coalition of labor leaders, energy producers, and nonprofits has voiced support for the permitting reform plan
quote.speaker: EPW Committee

items.outlet: Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee (Democrats)
items.author: Office of Sen. Martin Heinrich
items.title: What They're Saying: Heinrich's Bipartisan Permitting Reform Deal Will Deliver Cheaper Energy, More Jobs, Responsible Growth
items.summary: Heinrich's office circulated a supporter roundup and described the bill's data-center provision, which requires data centers to pay the full cost of their transmission needs.

quote.text: ensure that rapidly growing data centers pay the full cost of their associated transmission needs
quote.speaker: Office of Sen. Martin Heinrich (press release)

items.author: U.S. Senate
items.title: Senate floor log: pro forma sessions through November 5; Nov. 9 cloture vote on H.R. 2347
items.summary: The Senate floor log for October 15 lists pro forma sessions through November 5 and a November 9 cloture vote on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, the permitting vehicle.

quote.text: At approximately 5:30 p.m., the Senate will vote on cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R.2347
quote.speaker: U.S. Senate floor schedule

items.author: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito (@SenCapito)
items.title: The overwhelming support for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act speaks for itself
items.summary: Capito posted that the bill has broad support and urged passage.

quote.text: The overwhelming support for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act speaks for itself.
quote.speaker: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito

items.author: Joshua Siegel (@SiegelScribe)
items.title: E&C Chair Brett Guthrie says at Punchbowl Tech Summit he wants changes to the grid section
items.summary: Punchbowl reporter Joshua Siegel posted that House Energy and Commerce Chair Brett Guthrie would like changes to the bill's grid section.

quote.text: we absolutely would love to see changes to the
quote.speaker: Rep. Brett Guthrie (as reported by Joshua Siegel)

items.author: Brad McElhinny
items.title: Capito says permitting bill would blast away delays and protect approved projects
items.summary: Capito told MetroNews the White House made concessions on wind and solar projects and that she was promised a first vote when the Senate returns Nov. 8.

quote.text: The White House has been right here with us, has made some tremendous concessions
quote.speaker: Sen. Shelley Moore Capito

items.author: Jael Holzman
items.title: Jared Huffman Wants to See Some Changes to the Senate's Permitting Bill
items.summary: Huffman said no one would vote on the bill until after the election and called the bill's damages provision potentially a replay of settlements that bought out offshore wind projects.

quote.text: And no one is going to vote on this until after the election, anyway!
quote.speaker: Rep. Jared Huffman

items.author: Axios Future of Energy
items.title: How the permitting bill could collapse
items.summary: Axios's analysis of how the bill could collapse in a lame-duck session; it notes that the few definitive statements from lawmakers in both parties are supportive.

quote.text: The few definitive statements on the bill from lawmakers in both parties are supportive.
quote.speaker: Axios

items.author: Native American Rights Fund
items.title: ACT NOW: Senate Permitting Reform Bill Negatively Impacts Tribes
items.summary: NARF urged Tribal Nations to contact senators and said that, per its understanding, input must be received by October 23, while the Senate vote is not scheduled until November 9.

quote.text: we understand input must be received by October 23, and earlier the better.
quote.speaker: Native American Rights Fund

items.author: Coalition of 185 organizations (press release)
items.title: 185 Groups Slam Permitting Bill's Sweetheart Deal for Data Centers
items.summary: A coalition of 185 community, labor, climate and environmental justice groups urged congressional leaders to oppose the bill.

quote.text: urged congressional leaders to oppose anti-environmental permitting legislation
quote.speaker: Coalition of 185 groups (Center for Biological Diversity release)

items.author: Daily Caller News Foundation
items.title: Senators Want To Make AI Data Centers Pay For The Grid Upgrades Driving Up Your Electric Bill
items.summary: Reporting citing the AP says Sen. Mike Lee is confident the Senate will pass the bill in a lame-duck session in November.

quote.text: Lee said he is confident the Senate will pass it in a lame-duck session in November
quote.speaker: Sen. Mike Lee (as reported by AP)

events.title: Senate floor log sets Nov. 9 cloture vote on H.R. 2347, the permitting vehicle
events.summary: The October 15 floor log says the Senate is in pro forma sessions with no business through November 5, returns November 9 at 3:00 p.m., and votes on cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347 at about 5:30 p.m. The page titles H.R. 2347 the Survivor Justice Tax Prevention Act.
events.significance: Sets the procedural path: the House-passed H.R. 2347 is the vehicle for Senate text, and the first Senate step is a cloture vote on the motion to proceed.

sources.title: U.S. Senate Daily Press Gallery floor log

events.title: NARF says public input on the bill is due October 23
events.summary: NARF's alert says a Senate vote is not scheduled until November 9 but that, per its understanding, input must be received by October 23. NARF names no official Senate source for the October 23 date.
events.significance: The October 23 date is the only deadline for input found in the window, and it has no official source.
